boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Centre College
boards.description: Late-night dining options for Centre College students in Danville, ranging from on-campus cafes to local 24-hour staples.

cards.title: Late Night at the Flame
cards.subtitle: Roush Campus Center
cards.notes: Located on the first floor of the Roush Campus Center, this spot offers mobile ordering for late-night snacks until midnight daily.
cards.short_summary: On-campus retail dining venue offering late-night mobile ordering and pick-up for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Flame Café is open 7 days a week with mobile order/pick-up only from 9:00 pm to 12:00 midnight.
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight daily for mobile orders; accessible to students with meal plans or flex dollars.

cards.title: The 24-Hour Classic
cards.subtitle: Hustonville Road
cards.notes: A reliable 24/7 destination for breakfast food and late-night study breaks just a short drive from campus.
cards.short_summary: Iconic 24-hour diner serving breakfast and comfort food at all hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Waffle House locations are open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, including the Danville location.
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7; located approximately 1.5 miles south of the main campus.

cards.title: The Late-Night Tray
cards.subtitle: South Danville Bypass
cards.notes: Famous for its extensive milkshake menu and affordable trays, this drive-thru stays open until 3 AM or later.
cards.short_summary: Fast-food chain known for low-cost trays and late-night operating hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Cook Out is open until 3:00 AM or 4:00 AM on weekends, providing a primary late-night option for students.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru open until 3 AM Sunday-Thursday and 4 AM Friday-Saturday.

cards.title: Fourth Meal Run
cards.subtitle: Hustonville Road
cards.notes: A staple for late-night cravings, the drive-thru serves students until 3 AM most nights.
cards.short_summary: Popular fast-food destination for late-night Mexican-inspired fare.
cards.evidence_claim: The Taco Bell in Danville is open until 3:00 AM Sunday-Thursday and 4:00 AM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru open until 3 AM or 4 AM depending on the day.

cards.title: Midnight McNuggets
cards.subtitle: Jane Trail
cards.notes: The Jane Trail location provides late-night service for students seeking quick burgers and fries until midnight.
cards.short_summary: Global fast-food chain offering late-night drive-thru service in Danville.
cards.evidence_claim: McDonald's in Danville employs closers until 12:00 AM, indicating late-night availability.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru typically open until midnight.

cards.title: The Study Session Pizza
cards.subtitle: East Main Street
cards.notes: Conveniently located near campus, this Domino's is a go-to for late-night delivery during finals week.
cards.short_summary: Pizza delivery and carryout service located within walking distance of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino's on East Main Street offers delivery and carryout with hours extending late into the evening.
cards.access_notes: Open late for delivery and carryout; check app for specific nightly closing times.

cards.title: Late Night Slushes
cards.subtitle: Baughman Avenue
cards.notes: Students head here for half-price drinks and snacks, with the drive-in stalls open until midnight.
cards.short_summary: Drive-in restaurant offering a full menu and specialty drinks late into the night.
cards.evidence_claim: Sonic Drive-In in Danville is open until 12:00 AM daily.
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight every day of the week.

cards.title: The Frosty Run
cards.subtitle: Hustonville Road
cards.notes: A popular choice for a late-night Frosty or burger, with drive-thru service available until midnight.
cards.short_summary: Fast-food restaurant providing late-night drive-thru service on the south side of town.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy's on Hustonville Road has drive-thru hours until 12:00 AM daily.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru open until midnight daily.

cards.title: Late Night Sushi & Burgers
cards.subtitle: South Danville Bypass
cards.notes: A local favorite for late-night dining, offering a full menu of burgers and sushi until 11 PM or midnight.
cards.short_summary: Restaurant and bar with a diverse menu and late-night dining hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Drake's in Danville is open until 11:00 PM Sunday-Thursday and 12:00 AM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight on weekends; under-21 safe for dining.

cards.title: Late Night Carryout
cards.subtitle: West Main Street
cards.notes: Located just blocks from campus, this pizza spot is a frequent choice for late-night carryout orders.
cards.short_summary: Pizza chain offering delivery and carryout options near the Centre College campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Papa John's on West Main Street is open until 11:00 PM, serving as a late-evening option.
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:00 PM; located within walking distance of campus.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional student hubs and quiet corners of Centre College, from historic warehouse hangouts to modern collaborative labs and late-night study lounges.

cards.title: Collaborative Hub in Crounse Hall
cards.subtitle: Grace Doherty Library Main Floor
cards.notes: Visit this tech-savvy space for peer tutoring or group projects. It is located right next to Einstein Bros. Bagels for easy caffeine access during long study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A modern collaborative study area with peer tutoring and seminar rooms located inside the main library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Centre Learning Commons is located on the main floor of the Grace Doherty Library in Crounse Hall and includes spaces for individual and group study.
cards.access_notes: Open during Grace Doherty Library hours of operation; accessible to all students.

cards.title: Student Recreation and Billiards
cards.subtitle: Roush Campus Center
cards.notes: Check out pool balls or ping pong paddles at the Information Desk with your student ID. It is a popular spot for a quick break between classes or evening relaxation.
cards.short_summary: A central campus recreation space featuring pool tables and ping pong for student use.
cards.evidence_claim: Students can play pool and ping pong in the Campus Center by checking out equipment from the Information Desk with a photo ID.
cards.access_notes: Common areas are accessible 24 hours a day via student card swipe.

cards.title: Historic Hemp Warehouse Hangout
cards.subtitle: The Warehouse
cards.notes: Reserve the first floor for student events or meetings. This 1902 former hemp warehouse offers a unique industrial atmosphere for campus gatherings.
cards.short_summary: A renovated historic warehouse used for student meetings, recreation, and campus events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Combs Activities Center, known as the Warehouse, provides recreation, meeting space, and event space for the Centre community.
cards.access_notes: First floor available for student reservations via the Event Centre portal.

cards.title: Late Night Cardio and Weights
cards.subtitle: Sutcliffe Hall
cards.notes: Use your student ID for swipe access until midnight. The facility includes a cardio deck, weight room, and racquetball courts for all-day fitness.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus fitness facility offering extended hours for student workouts.
cards.evidence_claim: The Buck Fitness Center is open to Centre students with swipe card access from 5:00 am to 12:00 am daily.
cards.access_notes: Open daily until midnight; requires student ID for card swipe entry.

cards.title: STEM Study Nooks
cards.subtitle: Franklin W. Olin Hall
cards.notes: Find quiet study spots and innovative collaboration areas tucked between science labs. It is ideal for group work in chemistry or computer science.
cards.short_summary: Modern student-faculty collaborative spaces and quiet study areas within the science building.
cards.evidence_claim: Olin Hall features classrooms, faculty offices, and student/faculty collaborative spaces designed for optimal learning.
cards.access_notes: Accessible during academic building hours; primarily used by science and math students.

cards.title: Gold LEED Social Space
cards.subtitle: Pearl Hall Main Floor
cards.notes: Relax in the spacious main floor lounge or use the outdoor patio with a fire pit and grill. This LEED Gold certified building is a favorite for upperclassmen.
cards.short_summary: A high-efficiency social lounge and outdoor gathering area in a modern residence hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Pearl Hall features a spacious lounge on the main floor for social gatherings and a large patio area with a fire pit and grill.
cards.access_notes: Main lounge accessible to residents; common areas often host student life events.

cards.title: World-Class Shows for Free
cards.subtitle: Norton Center for the Arts
cards.notes: Scan your student ID at the Box Office starting at 6:30 p.m. on show nights for free admission. Arrive early as these limited tickets go fast.
cards.short_summary: A program providing Centre students free access to professional touring performances and concerts.
cards.evidence_claim: Centre students receive free tickets to Norton Center performances by scanning in at the Box Office beginning at 6:30 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Available on performance nights; student ID required for ticket pickup.

cards.title: Evening S'mores and Socials
cards.subtitle: Brockman Residential Commons
cards.notes: Gather at the courtyard fire pit for marshmallows and socializing. It is a key outdoor spot for upperclassmen living in the townhouse-style apartments.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor social hub featuring a fire pit and grill area for student gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Brockman Commons courtyard includes a fire-pit perfect for roasting marshmallows and socializing, plus an outdoor covered grill area.
cards.source_title: The A. Eugene Brockman Commons - Centre College
cards.access_notes: Outdoor courtyard is accessible to the campus community.

cards.title: Modern Science Lounge
cards.subtitle: Young Hall
cards.notes: Study in the open common areas of this Gold LEED building. The light-filled lobby and collaborative research labs provide a professional academic environment.
cards.short_summary: Sustainable and modern common areas designed for student-faculty collaborative research.
cards.evidence_claim: Young Hall features several new common areas to support student-faculty collaborative research and is Gold LEED certified.
cards.access_notes: Open during academic hours; common areas available for student study.

cards.title: Quiet Research and Printing
cards.subtitle: Grace Doherty Library
cards.notes: Head to the lower level for a 30-station computer lab and quiet research zones. It is often less crowded than the main floor Learning Commons.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated computer lab and quiet study zone located on the library's lower level.
cards.evidence_claim: A computer lab equipped with 30 desktop computers is available for research instruction and student use on the lower level of the library.
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; lower level is typically a designated quiet zone.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover free social spaces and activities at Centre College, from historic campus landmarks and modern study lounges to student-led weekend events and arts programming.

cards.title: Free Student Performance Tickets
cards.subtitle: World-class shows for zero dollars
cards.notes: Scan your student ID at the box office starting at 6:30 PM on show nights to claim a free ticket to regular series performances.
cards.short_summary: Centre students can attend high-profile concerts and theater productions at the Norton Center for free with a valid ID.
cards.evidence_claim: Regular series shows at the Norton Center are free to Centre students, with tickets available for pickup starting at 6:30 p.m. on performance nights.
cards.access_notes: Student tickets are limited and distributed on a first-come, first-served basis beginning 90 minutes before showtime.

cards.title: Study at the Doherty Library
cards.subtitle: Quiet research and social study bays
cards.notes: Access comfortable study areas and computer stations. The lobby often features rotating art exhibitions by students and professionals.
cards.short_summary: The main campus library offers multiple floors of free study space, research resources, and quiet zones for all students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Grace Doherty Library provides comfortable study areas, computer stations, and resources for students at no cost.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; check the library website for current academic term hours. A Centre ID is required to check out materials.

cards.title: SAC Late-Night Weekend Fun
cards.subtitle: Free campus-wide social events
cards.notes: Join the Student Activities Council for free weekend events including carnivals, live concerts, and themed late-night gatherings.
cards.short_summary: The SAC organizes a variety of free social events throughout the year, focusing on inclusive late-night weekend entertainment.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Activities Council (SAC) plans and organizes fun and inclusive events for the campus community for free.
cards.access_notes: Events are typically held in the Roush Campus Center or on the campus lawn and are open to all current students.

cards.title: Workout at Sutcliffe Hall
cards.subtitle: Free student gym access
cards.notes: Use your student ID to access the cardio deck, weight rooms, and indoor track. Open late most nights during the semester.
cards.short_summary: Located within Sutcliffe Hall, the Buck Fitness Center provides free gym and fitness facilities for the Centre community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Buck Fitness Center is open to Centre students, faculty, and staff with swipe card access at no additional cost.
cards.source_title: Sutcliffe Hall - Facilities - Centre College Athletics
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Sunday, 5:00 AM to 12:00 AM for students with valid card swipe access.

cards.title: Visit the Historic Old Centre
cards.subtitle: The heart of campus history
cards.notes: Walk through the 1819 Greek Revival building that served as a Civil War hospital. The second-floor Welcome Center is open to visitors.
cards.short_summary: Old Centre is the college's signature historic building, offering a free look at the institution's 19th-century roots.
cards.evidence_claim: Old Centre is the first building of the College and houses the Admission Office reception area, which is open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The building is open during standard administrative business hours, typically 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, Monday through Friday.

cards.title: Play Pool and Ping Pong
cards.subtitle: Free recreation in the student hub
cards.notes: Check out pool balls or ping pong paddles from the Information Desk for free. Limit play to 30 minutes if others are waiting.
cards.short_summary: The Campus Center game room offers free recreational equipment for students to use during building hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Students can check out pool and ping pong equipment from the Information Desk by leaving their Student ID.
cards.access_notes: Common areas are accessible to students 24 hours a day via card swipe; equipment checkout is available during desk hours.

cards.title: Collaborative Study at the CLC
cards.subtitle: Tech-savvy group work spaces
cards.notes: Located in Crounse Hall, this space offers free group study rooms and seminar spaces for collaborative projects.
cards.short_summary: The CLC provides modern, tech-equipped spaces for students to work together on academic projects at no cost.
cards.evidence_claim: The Centre Learning Commons includes innovative spaces for individual and group study and is open during library hours.
cards.access_notes: Located on the main floor of the Grace Doherty Library; accessible during standard library operating hours.

cards.title: Explore the Science Greenhouse
cards.subtitle: A quiet botanical escape
cards.notes: Visit the greenhouse located within the Young Hall science complex to see diverse plant collections used for biology research.
cards.short_summary: Young Hall features a greenhouse that serves as both a research facility and a unique, free indoor space to visit.
cards.evidence_claim: The renovated and expanded Young Hall includes a greenhouse as part of its science facilities.
cards.access_notes: Access is generally available during academic building hours; check with the Biology department for specific public viewing times.

cards.title: Disc Golf at Jackson Park
cards.subtitle: Free 9-hole PDGA course
cards.notes: Walk less than a mile from campus to play this 9-hole course. You can borrow discs for free from the Centre Recreation Office.
cards.short_summary: Henry Jackson Park offers a professional-grade disc golf course that is free for students and the local community.
cards.evidence_claim: Jackson Park offers a P.D.G.A. approved 9-hole course; discs can be obtained by contacting the Recreation Office.
cards.access_notes: The park is open to the public from dawn until dusk daily.

cards.title: Attend a Campus Convocation
cards.subtitle: Free lectures and cultural events
cards.notes: Attend designated convocation events for free to hear from guest speakers, authors, and performers while earning academic credit.
cards.short_summary: Convocations are free campus events that bring diverse perspectives to the student body through lectures and performances.
cards.evidence_claim: Centre Convocations are free for students and provide an hour of convocation credit for attendance.
cards.access_notes: Check the official convocation calendar for dates and locations; most are held in Newlin Hall or Weisiger Theatre.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Discover ten distinct study environments across the Centre College campus, from historic reading rooms to modern collaborative labs and outdoor classrooms.

cards.title: Library Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Crounse Hall
cards.notes: Reserve these rooms online via the library homepage for collaborative group work or focused team projects.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group study rooms located within the main campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: Students may reserve study rooms and seminar rooms on the Library home page.
cards.access_notes: Open 100.5 hours weekly; Centre ID required for checkout and reservations.

cards.title: Learning Commons Tech Spaces
cards.subtitle: Main Floor, Crounse Hall
cards.notes: Find innovative and tech-savvy spaces for individual and group study adjacent to the Einstein Bros. Bagels shop.
cards.short_summary: A modern, collaborative hub on the library's main floor featuring tech-equipped study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The space includes innovative and tech-savvy spaces for individual and group study, seminar rooms, and an information kiosk.
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; located on the main floor of Crounse Hall.

cards.title: Olin Hall STEM Collaboration Hub
cards.subtitle: Knowlton Center for Science and Mathematics
cards.notes: Utilize modern collaborative spaces designed for STEM students to work on complex data and science projects.
cards.short_summary: Collaborative study areas within the newly renovated science and mathematics center.
cards.evidence_claim: Classrooms, faculty offices, and student/faculty collaborative spaces are also located within Olin.
cards.access_notes: Primarily for STEM students but open for general academic use during building hours.

cards.title: Young Hall Late Night Labs
cards.subtitle: Rooms 134 and 213
cards.notes: Access dedicated computer labs for psychology and neuroscience research, open until midnight most nights.
cards.short_summary: Specialized computer labs in Young Hall available for late-night academic work.
cards.evidence_claim: Young Hall Computer Labs: 134, 213. Monday-Thursday: open 4 pm to midnight.
cards.access_notes: Open 4pm-midnight Mon-Thu; weekend hours vary.

cards.title: JVAC Creative Studios
cards.subtitle: West Walnut Street
cards.notes: Study in a unique environment surrounded by art; the building features purpose-built studios and a slide library.
cards.short_summary: Art-focused study and studio spaces in a renovated historic warehouse.
cards.evidence_claim: Classrooms, studios, a slide library, state-of-the-art hot glass studio, and faculty offices for the art department are located in JVAC.
cards.access_notes: Open to art students for studio work; general access during academic hours.

cards.title: Campus Center 24-Hour Lounges
cards.subtitle: Main Student Hub
cards.notes: Use your student ID for 24-hour card swipe access to common lounge areas for late-night study sessions.
cards.short_summary: Round-the-clock study lounges available to students in the main campus center.
cards.evidence_claim: The common areas of the building are accessible to students 24 hours a day by card swipe access.
cards.access_notes: 24-hour access for students via card swipe; public hours 8am-midnight.

cards.title: Historic Old Centre Classrooms
cards.subtitle: Main Administration Building
cards.notes: Study in one of the oldest college buildings in America; classrooms are available for student groups after hours.
cards.short_summary: Historic classroom and meeting spaces in the college's original 1820 building.
cards.evidence_claim: Classrooms in the academic buildings of the College are available to College groups, outside of class hours, for meetings and other purposes.
cards.access_notes: Available outside of scheduled class hours; online reservation required for groups.

cards.title: Grant Hall Music & Drama Studios
cards.subtitle: Norton Center for the Arts
cards.notes: Find quiet corners and academic studios in the academic wing of the Norton Center, home to music and drama programs.
cards.short_summary: Specialized academic and studio spaces for performing arts students.
cards.evidence_claim: Grant Hall, the academic wing of the Norton Center, is home to Centre College's music and drama programs. Complete with classrooms, studios and professional creative spaces.
cards.access_notes: Access for music and drama students; general academic use during building hours.

cards.title: Outdoor Academic Classrooms
cards.subtitle: Campus Grounds
cards.notes: Take your books outside to the Donald D. Buchanan or Elsie Wunsch outdoor classrooms for a fresh-air study session.
cards.short_summary: Designated outdoor spaces equipped for academic instruction and independent study.
cards.evidence_claim: Centre's campus features two outdoor classrooms where students enjoy an occasional outdoor classroom experience.
cards.access_notes: Open-air access; subject to weather and scheduled class use.

cards.title: Main Floor Quiet Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Crounse Hall
cards.notes: Seek out the quiet reading room on the main floor for a silent environment away from the Learning Commons' bustle.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated silent study area on the library's main floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Two quiet reading rooms on the main floor are often used for small, academic meetings as well as quiet study.
cards.access_notes: Open during regular library hours; designated for quiet study.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the historic streets and local businesses within walking distance of Centre College's campus in downtown Danville.

cards.entity_name: The Hub Coffee House and Cafe
cards.title: The Hub on Main Street
cards.subtitle: Main Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit this local coffeehouse to study or enjoy house-made pastries while looking out at the bustling downtown neighborhood.
cards.short_summary: A popular coffeehouse and student hangout on Danville's historic Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hub is described as a favorite hangout for faculty, staff, and students, featuring local art and house-made snacks.
cards.source_title: Your Centre College Visit - Visit Danville Kentucky
cards.access_notes: Open daily for coffee and light fare; check current hours for late-night study sessions.

cards.title: Dry Stack on Third Street
cards.subtitle: Third Street Corridor
cards.notes: Stop by this local roastery for fresh coffee, a highlight for first-year students during the Delve into Danville event.
cards.short_summary: A local coffee roastery and bar located on Third Street near the college.
cards.evidence_claim: Dry Stack Coffee Roastery + Coffee Bar is listed as a participating business in the Delve into Danville program for students.
cards.source_title: First-year students Delve into Danville | Centre College
cards.access_notes: Located on the one-way northbound stretch of 3rd Street.

cards.title: Constitution Square on Second
cards.subtitle: Second Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore the birthplace of Kentucky's statehood at this 3-acre park featuring historic log cabin replicas.
cards.short_summary: A historic park and open-air museum celebrating Kentucky's early political history.
cards.evidence_claim: Constitution Square is a 3-acre park in Danville that celebrates the early political history of Kentucky.
cards.access_notes: Public park open year-round; hosts the Great American Brass Band Festival.

cards.title: Fourth Street Development
cards.subtitle: Fourth Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this block near Main Street where the college has recently acquired property for future campus expansion.
cards.short_summary: A transitional commercial block connecting the campus to the downtown core.
cards.evidence_claim: Centre College reached an agreement to purchase a block near Main Street and Fourth Street for future development.
cards.source_title: Centre to buy block near Main St and Fourth St - Facebook
cards.access_notes: Public sidewalk access; area includes former bank and medical supply sites.

cards.title: Walnut Street Arts District
cards.subtitle: West Walnut Street
cards.notes: Attend world-class performances or view public art installations at this premier venue on the edge of campus.
cards.short_summary: Centre's primary performing arts venue located along West Walnut Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Norton Center for the Arts is located off of West Walnut Street and features public art and performances.
cards.source_title: First-year students Delve into Danville | Centre College
cards.access_notes: Parking is available behind the center off West Walnut Street.

cards.title: Mill Street Market Days
cards.subtitle: Mill Street Corridor
cards.notes: Browse local produce and handmade goods at the farmers market, a popular weekend destination for the campus community.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal market featuring local vendors and community engagement.
cards.evidence_claim: The Boyle County Farmer's Market is highlighted as a site of interest for students in the Delve into Danville program.
cards.source_title: First-year students Delve into Danville | Centre College
cards.access_notes: Check seasonal schedules for Saturday morning market hours.

cards.title: Lexington Avenue Literacy
cards.subtitle: Lexington Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Utilize the extensive resources and quiet study spaces at the public library, located just blocks from the college.
cards.short_summary: The local public library serving as a community and student resource.
cards.evidence_claim: The Boyle County Public Library is listed as a key community partner for Centre students.
cards.source_title: First-year students Delve into Danville | Centre College
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; students can obtain a local library card.

cards.title: Broadway Arts District
cards.subtitle: Broadway Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore regional art exhibits and participate in creative workshops at this community arts hub.
cards.short_summary: A regional art center offering galleries and educational programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Art Center of the Bluegrass is a highlighted cultural destination for the Centre community.
cards.source_title: First-year students Delve into Danville | Centre College
cards.access_notes: Galleries are generally free to the public; classes require registration.

cards.title: Maple Avenue Gateway
cards.subtitle: Maple Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Follow this historic route into town, passing local residences and small businesses that lead directly to the campus gates.
cards.short_summary: A primary residential and commercial artery leading to Centre College.
cards.evidence_claim: Maple Avenue (US-127 Business) is a main route for visitors traveling to the Admission Welcome Centre.
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; connects to Main Street at the college entrance.

cards.title: Second Street Heritage
cards.subtitle: South Second Street
cards.notes: Learn about the African-American history of the area through community events like the Soul of Second Street festival.
cards.short_summary: A historic district celebrating Danville's diverse cultural heritage.
cards.evidence_claim: The Soul of Second Street is an annual celebration of the African-American presence in the area around Constitution Square.
cards.access_notes: Public street; historical markers provide context for the district's significance.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From a chemical formula celebrating a historic football upset to a portrait that attends vice presidential debates, Centre College's traditions are deeply rooted in its 200-year Kentucky history.

cards.title: The Impossible Chemical Formula
cards.subtitle: Commemorating the 1921 Harvard Upset
cards.notes: Paint the formula C6H0 on campus surfaces to celebrate the 6-0 victory over Harvard. The notation was coined by a professor to suggest Harvard had been 'poisoned' by the score.
cards.short_summary: A symbolic chemical formula representing Centre's 6-0 football victory over Harvard in 1921.
cards.evidence_claim: The victory has been called 'one of the greatest upsets in sports history.' From that moment, C6H0 was born, representing Centre 6, Harvard 0.
cards.access_notes: Visible on various campus landmarks and athletic facilities.

cards.title: The Traveling Portrait of Fred Vinson
cards.subtitle: A Supreme Court Justice's Eternal Presence
cards.notes: Look for the portrait of alumnus and Chief Justice Fred Vinson at major events. He famously 'attended' the 2000 Vice Presidential debate held on campus with his own credential.
cards.short_summary: A portrait of Chief Justice Fred Vinson that is treated as a living guest at significant college events.
cards.evidence_claim: When Centre hosted the Vice-Presidential Debate in 2000, Dead Fred had his own special credential and was the first to be seated.
cards.access_notes: The portrait is maintained by the Phi Delta Theta fraternity and appears at campus-wide ceremonies.

cards.title: Passing the Talent
cards.subtitle: Commencement Eve Gratitude Ritual
cards.notes: Present a bronze 'talent' coin to a mentor who shaped your college journey. Seniors walk through Old Centre to the seal to hand off this symbolic token of appreciation.
cards.short_summary: A graduation tradition where seniors give a symbolic coin to a person who significantly impacted their education.
cards.evidence_claim: Graduates pause at the College seal to present a symbolic token to the individual they wish to honor for making a profound impact on their Centre Experience.
cards.access_notes: Held annually on the Old Centre lawn during Commencement weekend.

cards.title: Pennies for Lucky Lincoln
cards.subtitle: Exam Week Superstition
cards.notes: Leave a penny on the Abraham Lincoln statue before taking a final exam. The tradition honors the connection between Lincoln and his mentor, Centre alumnus John Todd Stuart.
cards.short_summary: A good-luck ritual involving leaving coins on a campus statue of Abraham Lincoln during finals.
cards.evidence_claim: Centre College on Instagram: 'Good luck with finals Centre students! Don't forget to visit "Lucky Lincoln" and leave a penny before your exams.'
cards.access_notes: The statue is located outdoors near the library and is accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Sealed with a Kiss
cards.subtitle: The Midnight Marriage Superstition
cards.notes: Kiss your partner on the brass seal in front of Old Centre at midnight. Legend says couples who do this are destined to marry after graduation.
cards.short_summary: A romantic campus legend involving a midnight kiss on the college's official seal.
cards.evidence_claim: College tradition holds that two students will marry at some point following graduation if, at the stroke of midnight, they kiss over the brass college seal.
cards.source_title: Sealed with a Kiss - Centre College Archives
cards.access_notes: The seal is embedded in the walkway in front of the Old Centre administration building.

cards.title: Spelling CENTRE with Your Body
cards.subtitle: The Global Photo Tradition
cards.notes: Gather a group to lie on the ground and form the letters C-E-N-T-R-E. This is a popular photo tradition for students studying abroad or visiting famous landmarks.
cards.short_summary: A tradition where students use their bodies to spell out the college's name in various locations.
cards.evidence_claim: Groups of Centre students seek out photo opportunities in which they use their bodies to spell 'CENTRE' in unique locations.
cards.access_notes: Performed spontaneously by students worldwide; no fixed location.

cards.title: Pancakes Served by Professors
cards.subtitle: Finals Week Fuel
cards.notes: Head to the dining hall during finals week for a late-night pancake feast. Faculty and staff volunteer to serve the meals as a show of support for stressed students.
cards.short_summary: An exam-week tradition where faculty serve breakfast foods to students late at night.
cards.evidence_claim: Late Night Breakfast is held each semester the night before final exams begin. It's served by faculty and staff and features music and pancakes.
cards.source_title: Late Night Breakfast at Centre College
cards.access_notes: Typically starts at 10:00 PM in the Cowan Dining Commons during finals week.

cards.title: Running the Flame
cards.subtitle: A Rite of Passage
cards.notes: Visit the 11-foot bronze sculpture that symbolizes the 'torch of knowledge.' It is the centerpiece of a long-standing (though officially discouraged) student running tradition.
cards.short_summary: A campus sculpture that serves as the focal point for a traditional student run.
cards.evidence_claim: The Flame, dedicated in 1969, is a symbolic representation of the torch of knowledge. Students began a tradition of running to The Flame and back.
cards.access_notes: Located in the center of campus in front of Crounse Hall.

cards.title: The Praying Colonels
cards.subtitle: A Unique Athletic Identity
cards.notes: Cheer for the 'Praying Colonels,' a nickname earned in the 1920s when the football team was known for praying before games. It remains the official mascot name today.
cards.short_summary: The unique official nickname of Centre College's athletic teams.
cards.evidence_claim: The yearbook of 1920 refers to the football team as the 'praying-fighting Colonels,' and the 1922 yearbook has the first use of the Praying Colonels.
cards.source_title: CentreCyclopedia - Nicknames and Colors - Centre College
cards.access_notes: Celebrated at all athletic events, particularly at Farris Stadium.

cards.title: The Civil War Hospital Legacy
cards.subtitle: A Building of Shared History
cards.notes: Tour the oldest college administration building west of the Alleghenies. During the Civil War, it served as a hospital for both Union and Confederate troops.
cards.short_summary: The historic heart of campus with a legacy as a wartime field hospital.
cards.evidence_claim: Old Centre served as everything from our first class building to a Civil War field hospital in its storied duration.
cards.access_notes: Houses administrative offices; the exterior and lawn are open to the public.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Centre College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Navigate your first days as a Colonel with this sequence of orientation traditions, campus landmarks, and essential student hangouts in Danville.

cards.title: Move-In and Check-In
cards.subtitle: Friday Morning Kickoff
cards.notes: Arrive between 9:00 AM and 12:00 PM to check into your residence hall and meet your First-Year Mentor who helps with the transition.
cards.short_summary: The official start of orientation where students move into campus housing and meet their mentors.
cards.evidence_claim: Move-in and check-in for new students is scheduled from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM on the first Friday of orientation.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation Schedule - Danville - Centre College
cards.access_notes: Open to incoming students and families during designated morning hours.

cards.title: Campus Connections Resource Fair
cards.subtitle: Friday Afternoon Discovery
cards.notes: Visit the resource fair from 3:00 PM to 4:00 PM to learn about campus organizations and student services available to you.
cards.short_summary: An afternoon fair introducing new students to various campus resources and involvement opportunities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Campus Connections Resource Fair is held from 3:00 PM to 4:00 PM on Friday afternoon during orientation.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation Schedule - Danville - Centre College
cards.access_notes: Held outdoors on the lawn or inside the Roush Campus Center depending on weather.

cards.title: Barb's Bodacious 80's Bash
cards.subtitle: Friday Night Social
cards.notes: Head to this themed social event starting at 9:00 PM to meet your classmates in a relaxed, high-energy environment.
cards.short_summary: A signature Friday night orientation social event featuring 1980s-themed music and activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Barb's Bodacious 80's Bash is a scheduled orientation event from 9:00 PM to 11:30 PM on Friday night.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation Schedule - Danville - Centre College
cards.access_notes: Late-night event specifically for orientation participants.

cards.title: Delve into Danville
cards.subtitle: Saturday Morning Exploration
cards.notes: Explore the local shops and murals of downtown Danville from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM to get familiar with your new home town.
cards.short_summary: A guided orientation program that introduces first-year students to the businesses and culture of downtown Danville.
cards.evidence_claim: The 'Delve into Danville' program is scheduled for Saturday morning from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation Schedule - Danville - Centre College
cards.access_notes: Walking tour starting from campus into the downtown district.

cards.title: Lunch at Cowan
cards.subtitle: The Main Dining Hub
cards.notes: Grab a meal at the Roush Campus Center; it's the primary all-you-care-to-eat destination for students on campus.
cards.short_summary: The central dining hall at Centre College, offering various food stations and communal seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Cowan Dining Commons is the main dining facility located within the Roush Campus Center.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; weekend hours are typically 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM.

cards.title: Live from Centre
cards.subtitle: Saturday Night Performance
cards.notes: Experience a live performance at Newlin Hall; students get free tickets to world-class touring acts throughout the year.
cards.short_summary: A premier performing arts venue on campus hosting concerts, theater, and student convocations.
cards.evidence_claim: The Norton Center for the Arts hosts orientation performances like 'Live from Centre' and provides free tickets to students.
cards.access_notes: Student ID required for free ticket scanning starting at 6:30 PM for evening shows.

cards.title: Centre Explore
cards.subtitle: Sunday Morning History
cards.notes: Tour the historic heart of campus, including Old Centre, which has served the college since its opening in 1820.
cards.short_summary: A morning orientation session focused on navigating campus facilities and learning college history.
cards.evidence_claim: The 'Centre Explore' session is held Sunday morning from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM during orientation.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation Schedule - Danville - Centre College
cards.access_notes: Focuses on administrative and historic buildings near the main lawn.

cards.title: Workout at Sutcliffe Hall
cards.subtitle: Afternoon Recreation
cards.notes: Use your student ID to swipe into the fitness center for a workout; it's open until midnight most days.
cards.short_summary: The primary student fitness facility featuring weight rooms, cardio equipment, and courts.
cards.evidence_claim: The Buck Fitness Center in Sutcliffe Hall is open to students with swipe access from 5:00 AM to 12:00 AM daily.
cards.source_title: Fitness Center General - Centre College Athletics
cards.access_notes: Student ID required for entry; Sunday hours for the main hall are 1:00 PM to 8:00 PM.

cards.title: Hollywood Casino Night
cards.subtitle: Sunday Night Entertainment
cards.notes: Join the class for a night of mock-casino games and social interaction at the Combs Center from 9:00 PM to 11:00 PM.
cards.short_summary: A popular orientation social event featuring non-monetary casino games and prizes.
cards.evidence_claim: Hollywood Casino Night is a scheduled orientation activity on Sunday night from 9:00 PM to 11:00 PM.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation Schedule - Danville - Centre College
cards.access_notes: Late-night event for students; no real gambling involved.

cards.title: Coffee at Einstein's
cards.subtitle: Monday Morning Prep
cards.notes: Visit Crounse Hall to find the library and the adjacent Einstein Bros. Bagels, a favorite spot for coffee and study sessions.
cards.short_summary: The main campus library which also houses the Centre Learning Commons and a popular bagel shop.
cards.evidence_claim: Einstein Bros. Bagels is located on the main floor of the Grace Doherty Library in Crounse Hall.
cards.access_notes: Einstein's is open Monday-Friday starting at 7:30 AM.
